Below are five AI-generated responses to the same task, labelled A through E.

Each response was written by one of these five language models:
GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek.

For each of the five responses, identify which model you believe wrote it, judging only from writing style, structure, and phrasing.

Answer independently for each response. Your five answers do not need to be five different models - name whichever model you believe wrote each response, even if that means naming the same model more than once.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this form and nothing else:

{
  "A": {"model": "<one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek>", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"},
  "B": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "C": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "D": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "E": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."}
}

confidence: 1 = pure guess, 5 = certain.

--- RESPONSE A ---
A black hole is an extremely dense region in space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from it. It forms when a massive star collapses under its own gravity at the end of its life, creating a point of infinite density called a singularity. The boundary around a black hole, called the event horizon, marks the point of no return for anything that gets too close.

--- RESPONSE B ---
A black hole is a region of space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape once it gets too close. This boundary is called the event horizon. Black holes can form when very massive stars collapse, and they can also grow by pulling in gas, dust, and other matter around them.

--- RESPONSE C ---
A black hole is a region of space where gravity is so intense that nothing, not even light, can escape once it crosses a boundary called the event horizon. They typically form when massive stars collapse under their own gravity at the end of their lives, compressing enormous amounts of matter into an incredibly small volume. At their center lies a singularity, a point where known physics breaks down and density becomes effectively infinite. Although black holes themselves are invisible, astronomers detect them by observing their gravitational effects on nearby stars and the superheated gas that spirals into them.

--- RESPONSE D ---
A black hole is an area in space where gravity is so incredibly strong that nothing, not even light, can escape its pull. This extreme gravity usually forms when a massive star dies and collapses in on itself, squeezing a huge amount of matter into an unimaginably tiny space. Because no light can escape, these objects are invisible, but scientists can detect them by observing how their powerful pull affects nearby stars and gas.

--- RESPONSE E ---
A black hole is a region in space where gravity has become so powerful that nothing, not even light, can escape once it crosses a certain boundary. These objects usually form when a massive star runs out of fuel and collapses under its own weight at the end of its life. The intense gravity pulls in nearby gas, stars, and light, often creating detectable effects like swirling disks of hot material or distorted paths of light around them.

--- END OF RESPONSES ---
